written: 2026-09-27, before any of C1 or C2 was computed; C3 was seen in research/2026-09-returns-study (post-hoc)
hypothesis: A simple core book can replace Meridian's eight sleeves without losing risk-adjusted performance (non-inferiority, not a skill claim).
benchmark: BASELINE: honest fund B from research/2026-09-returns-study/step1_baseline.py (current weights; momentum on SPY QQQ IWM EFA EEM GLD IEF TLT; trend on SPY; single-stock sleeves in T-bills; SVXY vix_band; long_term_etf and sector_rotation as live).

candidates.C1: 50% 60/40 SPY/IEF (monthly rebalance) + 25% long_term_etf live model (ma_bond_rotation_cs_b126 on QQQ IEF KMLM) + 25% T-bills
candidates.C2: 50% Faber 10-month rule on SPY EFA IEF GSG VNQ (as research/plans/faber_gtaa_5etf.json) + 25% long_term_etf live model + 25% 60/40 SPY/IEF
candidates.C3: POST-HOC: current weights; sector_rotation, momentum and trend_following held (equal weight of their instruments) instead of timed; single-stock sleeves in T-bills; 5% cash in T-bills

data: Total returns (adj_close), 10 bps per side, T-bills = ^IRX/252 lagged a day, long-only

pass_rule.tie_break: fewest sleeves, then highest full-period Sharpe

honesty_note: All of 2011-2026 was seen during 2026-09-27 research. This compares structures on known history; the live record after any switch is the real test.

consequences.one_or_more_non_inferior: Propose the winner as Meridian's core book at the owner's chosen drawdown target, retire the no-edge sleeves to research, and switch only with the owner's OK (at the ~10/11 review or earlier on explicit instruction).
consequences.none_non_inferior: Keep the current structure; still retire the single-stock sleeves and SVXY if the owner agrees, since they showed no honest edge.
